question: Why does band-anchors.test.ts pin BAND_ANCHORS twice, once as five inline strings and once as bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS), when either assertion alone fails on an anchor edit?

items.text: **AC-10**: A committed test (no vendor call, runs under the ordinary free unit suite) asserts `BAND_ANCHORS` literally equals today's text (`toEqual` against the five strings written inline in the test, never a snapshot file, which a routine `vitest -u` could silently rewrite) and that `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)` equals today's computed hash, both failing by name and naming spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes,

**Done by spec 0017's AC-10**, and by the concrete way this item names: `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors.test.ts` pins the anchor wording, and its failure message names this dataset and `pairs.ts` by path, telling the reader to re-argue each affected pair rather than update the expectation. A second assertion pins `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)`, which is the value written into every eval report, so a change to the hash function alone is caught as well. It runs in the free unit suite, so drift is caught by `pnpm test`.

Add the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test under `src/features/scoring/eval/` (the ordinary unit project, no vendor call): a literal `toEqual` pin of today's text plus a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, both failing by name, pointing at spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes. Satisfies **AC-10**.

If feature 16's eval harness later shows the five bands clustering rather than spreading (the condition **AC-2** defers to that harness), the band anchors in `rubric.ts` are the first thing to revise, not the vendor or any of this prompt's other instructions. **Still open, and its trigger has not fired.** Feature 16's harness ran the full sixteen pairs twice on 2026-09-08 and both runs observed all five bands, `strong_match` 35, `good_match` 5, `possible_match` 21, `weak_match` 11, `not_a_match` 8 in the first and 35, 4, 21, 8, 12 in the second, so the bands spread rather than clustered and AC-2's bar of at least three of five was already met. Spec 0018 did review the anchors, but for a different reason, two pairs disagreeing with their recorded expectation, and it concluded that `BAND_ANCHORS` holds and one committed expectation was wrong. No anchor changed and the hash is still `1b45f524b356`. So this item is neither satisfied nor superseded by that review; it is waiting on a clustering condition that has not been seen.

**What is unchanged and why it matters**: `BAND_ANCHORS`, the anchor hash `1b45f524b356`, the drift guard, `scoreListing()`, the response schema, the five `Band` values, and every other pair's expectation.

**AC-9**: v1 shows `job_search` usage only, and this is a proven choice, not a deferred one. `src/features/search/adzuna.ts`'s `RESULTS_PER_PAGE` is exported so a test can import the real value rather than a copied literal. That test, run against the real `usage_cap` rows (an integration test, since the caps are no deploy editable per AC-5 and a unit test could only pin the migration's seed values), asserts that `ai_scoring`'s and `ai_check`'s own caps stay at or above `job_search`'s own cap times `RESULTS_PER_PAGE`, for all three window scopes (account week, global day, global month), not only the one this feature displays. That arithmetic is what guarantees `job_search`'s own cap always binds at or before either AI tier's, so showing it alone tells the whole truth about what will actually stop the caller. The test failing, or an operator changing a cap value so it no longer holds, is the signal to revisit this scope.
`control-one-gap`'s recorded expectation is wrong under the anchor text that already exists, so the pair is corrected and `BAND_ANCHORS` is not touched.
`BAND_ANCHORS` and its hash `1b45f524b356` are untouched,

**AC-9**: The command writes a JSON report every run, in addition to the console table, to a directory this repository does not track, at `test/eval/.output/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced by dashes>.json`, creating that directory if it does not exist. Each report is a single `EvalReport` object (defined in `test/eval/report.ts`) recording: the filter used (if any) and every skipped pair id; per pair, its status (`pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`), sub reason where relevant, denominator, and every observed band (or band distribution); the preference leak check's own outcome; the run's overall status and aborted reason if any; and, once per report, which model answered (via the shared `resolvedModel()` guard on `TIERS.ai_scoring.model`, never a name typed into the harness) and a hash of `BAND_ANCHORS`'s current text (`bandAnchorsHash()`, defined once and shared with the AC-10 test, so "the same way" is true by construction rather than by two separate implementations agreeing).

**AC-1**: `src/features/scoring/rubric.ts` defines five ordered, named bands (`strong_match`, `good_match`, `possible_match`, `weak_match`, `not_a_match`), each carrying a written anchor description sent verbatim in the prompt,

**AC-12**: The prompt's system instructions state that the listing's title and description are untrusted external text, that the model must not follow any instruction contained within them, and must not fetch, describe, or act on any URL or address that appears in them.

**AC-13**: The prompt built from the caller's profile is bounded regardless of how much the user wrote: the full `summary` (already capped at 4000 characters, spec 0010 AC-3), at most 50 skills (in `readProfileSections()`'s own `lower(name)` ascending order, the same 50 value ceiling this project already uses for `job_preference`'s own list fields, spec 0010 AC-9), the full `job_preference` row when present (already bounded by spec 0010 AC-9's own limits, no new cap needed), and at most the 5 most recent `work_experience` entries in the order `readProfileSections()` already returns them, each entry's own `description` truncated to 300 characters before it enters the prompt. When a listing's own `descriptionSnippet` is absent (an optional field, spec 0013), the prompt states plainly that no description was returned for this posting and the model reasons from the title alone.

**AC-2**: Across the genuinely varied listings feature 15's ground truth set will author, scored results spread across at least three of the five bands rather than clustering on one. This is exercised by feature 16's eval harness once feature 15 exists, not by this feature's own unit tests,

**AC-4**: The prompt built for every listing states plainly that Adzuna truncates `descriptionSnippet` at 500 characters and marks a truncated description with a trailing "…"; the model is instructed never to assert that a skill is required by a specific posting unless the visible text actually says so, and never to treat an unconfirmed skill as absent from the posting either.

**AC-5**: The score schema exposes `matchedSkills` (the caller's own skills whose name, or a clear synonym, appears in the listing's visible title or description) and `notMentionedSkills` (skills from the caller's own list that a role like this one would typically value, that do not appear anywhere in the listing's visible text). Both arrays are filtered after parsing to names that case insensitively match one of the caller's own `profile_skill` names; any other name the model returns is dropped before it reaches the UI, never displayed and never a reason to fail the whole call. Neither the schema field name nor any displayed label ever reads "missing skills"; the UI's label for `notMentionedSkills` states plainly that this is not a confirmed absence (`COPY-2`).

**AC-6**: A `sponsorshipSignal` field is a required enum of `sponsors`, `does_not_sponsor`, or `not_stated`, resolved from whether the listing's visible text states a sponsorship stance explicitly. `not_stated` renders nothing on the card, the same visible outcome an absent field would have had, The signal is never used to compute or adjust the band, and when present (`sponsors` or `does_not_sponsor`) it renders as its own separate badge, distinct from the band badge (`COPY-6`).

**AC-3**: `full_name` is required and at most 200 characters. `summary` is optional and at most 4000 characters. `location` is optional. A submission that fails a rule writes nothing and returns a visible error next to the field, with the values the user typed kept in place.

**AC-9**: Search preferences (`desired_titles`, `desired_locations`, `remote_preference`, `minimum_pay`, `minimum_pay_currency`) are edited together as one section. `desired_titles` and `desired_locations` are each entered as one field, one value per line, never comma separated (a location value can itself contain a comma); each line is trimmed, empty lines are dropped, values are deduplicated ignoring case the same way skills are, each value is at most 100 characters, and each list holds at most 50 values. `remote_preference` is a closed choice among `on_site`, `hybrid`, `remote`, `no_preference`. `minimum_pay` and `minimum_pay_currency` are both present or both absent; an empty `minimum_pay` field is treated as absent before that pairing check runs, never as zero. When present, `minimum_pay` is at least 0, at most 9,999,999,999.99, and at most two decimal places, rejected rather than rounded; `minimum_pay_currency` is a free text field, trimmed and uppercased before checking, then exactly three uppercase letters, with no fixed currency list (the schema has none, and one here would be a second source of truth).

claims.text: The two assertions guard different things. The inline `toEqual` pins the anchor wording, and the hash assertion pins `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)`, which is the value written into every eval report. A change to the hash function alone is therefore caught too, even if the anchor text is untouched.
The inline strings are used instead of a snapshot file because a routine `vitest -u` could silently rewrite a snapshot. The hash is checked against today's computed value.

The hash is defined once and shared between the report and the drift test, so the report's hash and the test's hash are computed the same way by construction. Pinning it in the test therefore protects the value that reports carry for comparison.

The wording pin exists because the anchors' own comment says the wording is expected to change, and every expected band and rationale in the ground truth set derives from today's wording. Spec 0016 asked the harness spec to detect that drift, and AC-10 is the item that does so.
The build step for the drift test satisfies AC-10 with both a literal `toEqual` pin and a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, each failing by name and pointing at spec 0016's dataset.
